r.methodCommitTable:
Per-method commit/tie-break (cited [LIT], in /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/FR13_TREE_VERIFY_LITERATURE.md §1):
- SpecInfer (2305.09781): token-tree verify; greedy = longest root-to-leaf path where every token==target argmax (top-down); stochastic = multi-step speculative sampling (recursive residual norm(relu(p-q)), Thm 4.1/4.2 lossless). Tie-break: descending draft prob / first matching child. Assumes verify==target; NO realization-gap notion.
- Sequoia (2402.12374): sampling-WITHOUT-replacement verify loop (optimal-transport k=1 + cover property) -> provably exact target dist across temps; greedy reduces to longest-prefix. Tie by draft prob. Assumes verify==target; no batched-vs-sequential drift notion.
- SpecTr: multi-draft optimal-transport acceptance, lossless by OT coupling. Assumes verify==target.
- EAGLE/-2/-3: dynamic tree, accept longest prefix matching target's own predictions (argmax greedy / SpS sampling), 'no impact on accuracy'. Tie = top-down longest-accepted prefix, higher-confidence branch preferred. Assumes verify==target (dense single-seq => verify==decode by construction); no realization-gap notion.
- Medusa (2401.10774): tree-attn + TYPICAL-ACCEPTANCE = longest prefix clearing a prob/entropy threshold, NOT exact argmax => LOSSY by design ('not insisting on exact correspondence').
- DeFT (2404): IO/HBM-efficient flash tree-attention KERNEL only (prefix-aware, load-balanced KV); not a commit rule; relevant as the no-extra-HBM shared-prefix reference for our 273 GB/s bound.
- STree (2505.14969): speculative tree decoding for hybrid SSMs (our exact regime); packed-tree reusing accumulated state-transition matrices; standard accept on top. Assumes the SSM tree forward==sequential forward; does NOT claim tree-batched realization == per-path recurrent realization -> closest paper to our carrier, with no realization-gap remedy.
- Traversal Verification (2505.12398): bottom-up leaf->root sequence-level chain accept; temp>0 ONLY (greedy explicitly excluded App. G); assumes verify==target (Lemma A.2); no realization-gap notion.
- vLLM rejection_sampler (v1): temp>0 per-token rejection sampling + recovery norm(relu(p-q)); temp=0 = pure argmax (ties->lowest index); 'greedy spec == greedy non-spec' equality test is SAME-ENGINE so does NOT cover our GDN tree-batched-vs-recurrent gap. Assumes verify==target.
- SGLang (EAGLE): tree expanded by eagle_topk, reranked, longest accepted path; EXPOSES --speculative-accept-threshold-single/-acc = optional LOSSY typical-acceptance knobs (off=lossless). Assumes verify==target.
- MARS (2601.15498): margin-aware = relaxes rejection at low target margin, accepts a RUNNER-UP draft token => LOSSY relative to strict token verification (abstract decisive; full PDF was binary-blocked).
UNANIMOUS finding [INF over LIT]: every losslessness theorem assumes verify forward dist IS the target dist; NONE handles verify-vs-target/decode drift, because in a dense single-seq Transformer verify==decode by construction. Our GDN tree-batched leaf-co-resident recurrent forward breaks that identity -> our problem is not in the literature. Lossy outliers (Medusa typical-accept, MARS runner-up, SGLang thresholds) are BANNED for us (runner-up/top-k/threshold = LOSSY reward-hack).
r.spineBonusLosslessVerdict:
VERDICT: a deterministic prefer-canonical-path / spine-bonus / margin-aware tie-break is PROVABLY LOSSLESS for greedy temp-0 tree spec decoding ONLY when the deciding node is a SUB-FLOOR near-tie, and LOSSY otherwise. It is NOT a literature-named method for the realization-gap case; it is a SOUND NOVEL tie-break [INF] composing two cited facts: (1) greedy verify is lossless iff committed token==target argmax (EAGLE/vLLM greedy-equality); (2) our floor is MEASURED not zero (native non-deterministic, B=4 bag-TV 0.113), so two tokens whose verify logits differ by less than the floor are indistinguishable to the target.
EXACT MARGIN RULE: at a fork where leaf_lcp strictly exceeds spine_lcp, let m = verify_top2_margin at the deciding node = argmax_logit - runnerup_logit of the VERIFY row the committer used (runner-up = spine's token; this is already computed by our CAG instrument as verify_top2_margin). If m <= FLOOR (verify nearly indifferent, spine token is the runner-up within the realization floor): committing the SPINE is LOSSLESS (target cannot resolve the order below the floor; bug-class #11 sub-ULP). If m > FLOOR (verify confidently prefers the leaf token over spine): committing the spine is LOSSY = rejecting a real accept. FLOOR is the per-node logit-margin counterpart of the bag-TV 0.113 floor and must be MEASURED as the p95 top-2 margin on a native-vs-native same-seed control arm at the same shape (bug-class #12: never hard-code, never single-draw 0.0593).
CONTRAST: MARS (runner-up) and Medusa typical-acceptance are LOSSY because they relax accept for SPEED even when the target has a clear preference. Spine-bonus is the opposite asymmetry: it only ever DECLINES a leaf toward the canonical spine, and only within the floor, so it never accepts a token the target disprefers. That asymmetry is why it can be lossless where MARS/top-k cannot. NOVELTY: margin-gated determinism is standard; what is novel is gating it by the verify-vs-decode REALIZATION FLOOR (no surveyed paper has that object).
r.traversalVerificationAssessment:
Traversal Verification (2505.12398): bottom-up leaf->root; per chain cumulative accept probs root->leaf; sample eta~U(0,1); accept ENTIRE leaf-to-root chain if eta < p_alpha(leaf-path); else delete leaf, redistribute residual/draft mass, recompute siblings; iterate. Theorem 3.3 = output equals target dist. It IS committer-only / plug-and-play: reorders which path is committed from the SAME single verify forward, NO re-inference, NO KV/state copy, NO extra HBM traffic -> fits our 273 GB/s constraint on that axis.
Does it avoid our leaf-fork? NO, not the way we need, three disqualifiers [INF]: (1) temp>0 ONLY -- greedy EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED (App. G: 'all verification approaches functionally equivalent' at t=0); our binding bar is greedy argmax vs the decode oracle, and the user ruling is greedy-branch-rescue is the real bar, so Traversal is inert exactly where we need it. (2) Assumes verify==target (Lemma A.2), NO realization-gap notion -> on our GDN forward it commits leaf chains the decode oracle never produces, the SAME trajectory fork, just bottom-up; solves nothing about verify-vs-decode. (3) The fork it 'avoids' is the OPPOSITE of ours: its advantage is salvaging valid child subsequences a rejected parent would discard (it commits MORE off-spine chains), whereas we are OVER-committing leaves -> it would INCREASE our forks.
Strictly better than spine-bonus? For greedy (our bar) NO (inert + wrong direction). For temp>0 superset/speed (deferred) it is a genuinely attractive committer-only no-copy no-HBM acceptance-LENGTH upgrade -> prefer it LATER as the temp>0 path-acceptance layer, but ONLY after the realization gap is otherwise closed (else it inherits the fork). It is COMPLEMENTARY to spine-bonus, not a substitute: spine-bonus fixes WHICH near-tie token greedy commits; Traversal fixes HOW MANY tokens a sampling run accepts. WY stays PARKED.
r.mappingToOurLCP:
Our committer (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py L6818-6976): lcp = longest prefix where drafts[node]==parent_targets[node] (parent_targets=argmax of the VERIFY forward at the node); best_path=argmax lcp; tie-break=earliest flattened leaf, and because vLLM emits SORTED trees the spine is earliest, so spine ALREADY wins on EQUAL lcp (L6917-6923). The fork is strictly leaf_lcp > spine_lcp.
Spine-on-EQUAL-lcp = exactly the EAGLE/vLLM deterministic canonical-path tie-break [LIT], uncontroversially lossless. Extending to leaf_lcp>spine_lcp BUT within the floor = the margin rule above: lossless-within-floor and a SOUND NOVEL tie-break [INF] -- it only declines a leaf where the verify top-2 margin m<=FLOOR, i.e. where the verify forward itself could not resolve leaf-vs-spine above the realization floor; at such a node the leaf 'win' is a verify-realization artifact (bug-class #11/#12) not a target preference, so committing the canonical (spine) token is lossless w.r.t. the DECODE ORACLE -- which is the actual bar (the literature's verify==target identity is exactly what is broken at these nodes, so 'lossless w.r.t. the verify forward', which raw LCP already is, is the WRONG target here).
DOES IT NEED THE PROBE? YES. The principled fix is CONDITIONAL: damp the spine->leaf boundary only where m<=FLOOR. To deploy it lossless we must confirm via the GPU committer-margin probe that the forks are sub-floor, and bin any m>FLOOR forks as FUNDAMENTAL (NOT spine-bonus-fixable; genuine verify-vs-decode divergence at a confident node, must be closed upstream, never damped). A BLANKET spine-bonus that fires regardless of margin would be LOSSY (rejects confident leaf accepts) and is BANNED as a reward-hack, same class as FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT (already documented DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY 'NEVER bind =1', L6855-6867). Instrument is already in place: the CAG block L7007-7125 computes per served token verify_top2_margin and ch1_margin and tags node_type spine/leaf + winner_path_idx vs spine_path_idx; the probe just histograms those across the 23 forks to decide the floor split.

v.spineBonusSound: HOLDS and is logically sound, not hand-waved. The verdict states spine-bonus is PROVABLY LOSSLESS for greedy temp-0 ONLY when the deciding node is a SUB-FLOOR near-tie, and LOSSY otherwise (suppressing a confident genuine leaf win = rejecting a real accept). The exact margin condition is stated precisely: at a fork where leaf_lcp strictly exceeds spine_lcp, m = verify_top2_margin (argmax_logit - runnerup_logit of the verify row, runner-up = spine token, already computed by the CAG instrument); if m <= FLOOR commit spine = LOSSLESS, if m > FLOOR commit spine = LOSSY. FLOOR is correctly required to be MEASURED (multi-sample p95 of a native-vs-native control arm, the per-node logit counterpart of bag-TV 0.113), NOT hard-coded (bug-class #12). It does NOT smuggle a lossy top-k/runner-up accept: the asymmetry is explicit and correct — spine-bonus only ever DECLINES a leaf toward the canonical spine within the floor (never accepts a token the target disprefers), the opposite direction from MARS/Medusa which relax accept for speed at confident margins. Novelty claim is honest: margin-gated determinism is standard; gating by the verify-vs-decode REALIZATION floor is the novel object (no surveyed paper has it). The "lossless w.r.t. decode oracle (the actual bar), not w.r.t. verify forward (which raw LCP already is)" distinction is exactly right and is the crux.
v.traversalSound: HOLDS and is grounded in the actual paper, not invented. I fetched the arXiv HTML and confirmed verbatim: bottom-up leaf-to-root traversal, the eta~U(0,1) / eta<p_alpha(leaf-path) chain-accept test, the delete-leaf + redistribute-residual-to-siblings + recompute mechanism, Theorem output==target, and crucially the App. G greedy-exclusion. The committer-only / no-copy / no-HBM claim is CORRECT: it reorders which path is committed from the SAME single verify forward (no re-inference, no KV/state copy, no extra HBM) so it fits the 273 GB/s constraint on that axis. The three disqualifiers for OUR case are sound: (1) temp>0 ONLY, greedy explicitly excluded -> inert at our binding greedy bar; (2) assumes verify==target (Lemma A.2), no realization-gap notion -> commits leaf chains the decode oracle never produces (same fork, just bottom-up); (3) it pushes toward MORE off-spine chain commits (salvaging deeper accepts) = the OPPOSITE direction from our over-committing-leaves carrier, so it would INCREASE forks. v.recommendation: The spine-bonus IS a principled, sound, novel margin-gated tie-break that is lossless-within-floor — but it is NOT unconditionally deployable: the recommendation correctly makes it CONDITIONAL and REQUIRES the GPU committer-margin probe sub-floor confirmation before binding. The principled fix damps the spine->leaf boundary ONLY where m <= FLOOR; any fork with m > FLOOR must be binned as FUNDAMENTAL (genuine verify-vs-decode divergence at a confident node, closed upstream, NEVER damped), and a blanket spine-bonus firing regardless of margin is correctly flagged LOSSY and banned (same class as FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT, which the code documents DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY "NEVER bind =1", L6855-6867 confirmed). Traversal Verification is NOT the better committer for our greedy bar (it is inert at temp-0 and pushes the wrong direction); it is complementary and banked as a future temp>0 upgrade only. So: spine-bonus = the right lever for the greedy carrier, gated on probe sub-floor confirmation; Traversal = deferred temp>0 layer. Note the bimodal probe result already in the prior commit c1004bc3 (10 sub-floor near-ties spine-bonus-fixable + 13 confident leaf-wins fundamental) is consistent with this verdict — i.e. spine-bonus alone gets ~23->~15, not native-3, the residual being confident leaf-wins that are NOT spine-bonus-fixable.
